user.title: Powerwall TEDAPI
user.description: How should Home Assistant connect to your Powerwall? Signed (v1r) access gives local readings, local control and battery dispatch. It needs a key registered with your Powerwall once, which this wizard can do.

menu_options.existing_key: Use a key that is already registered

login.title: Sign in to Tesla
login.description:
Your Tesla account is used to register the key with the Powerwall and as a backup for changing settings when the local connection is down.

1. Open this link on a computer, with the browser's developer tools open on the **Network** tab (F12):
   [Sign in to Tesla]({url})
2. Sign in. The last page will not load, because Tesla sends the browser to a `tesla://auth/callback?code=…` address.
3. In the Network tab, find the request starting with `callback?code=` (or the `Location` header of the last redirect) and copy that full address.
4. Paste it below. Codes expire within minutes and work once.

verify.title: Confirm at the Powerwall
verify.description:
The key (fingerprint `{fingerprint}…`) is registered and waiting for physical confirmation. Within about 10 minutes:

- **Powerwall 3:** switch the On/Off switch (left side, under the red rapid-shutdown flap) OFF for about 15 seconds, then back ON. A short flick is ignored; leaving it off until the unit powers down closes the window.
- **Other models:** toggling the Powerwall's AC breaker off for about 15 seconds is reported to work on some units.

Then select **Submit**. Checking takes up to a minute.

connect_v1r.title: Connect to the Powerwall (signed)
connect_v1r.description:
**Gateway address:** the Powerwall's address on your home network (find it in your router, and reserve it), or the Powerwall's own Wi-Fi hotspot `192.168.91.1` if Home Assistant is connected to that network.

**Wi-Fi fallback:** the hotspot address, used over the same signed connection when the home-network address stops answering. Leave it empty if Home Assistant cannot reach the hotspot.

data.cloud_backup: Link a Tesla account as a backup for settings

data_description.gw_pwd: The password printed on the QR sticker inside the Powerwall's cover. Not needed for signed access.
data_description.rsa_key_path: PEM file of a key registered with `python -m pypowerwall register` (state VERIFIED).

connect_wifi.title: Connect over the Powerwall's Wi-Fi
connect_wifi.description: Home Assistant must be connected to the Powerwall's own Wi-Fi network (TeslaPW_…). This connection can read everything but cannot change settings or dispatch the battery; link a Tesla account to change settings through the cloud.

data.cloud_backup: Link a Tesla account to change settings

data_description.gw_pwd: The password printed on the QR sticker inside the Powerwall's cover.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Give an RSA key file to use the signed (v1r) connection; leave it empty for the Wi-Fi password connection.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Powerwall at that address.
error.invalid_rsa_key: No key file at that path.
error.key_not_accepted: The Powerwall did not accept the key. Check that it is registered and VERIFIED for this Powerwall.
error.invalid_auth: Tesla did not accept that code. A new sign-in link has been made; sign in again and paste the new address.
error.cloud_error: The Tesla service returned an error. Try again in a minute.
error.not_verified: The Powerwall has not confirmed the key yet. Do the switch step, wait a few seconds, then submit again.
error.verify_timeout: The 10-minute window closed. Submit to register the key again, then do the switch step.

abort.already_configured: This Powerwall is already set up.
abort.no_sites: No Powerwall was found on this Tesla account.
abort.register_failed: The Powerwall did not accept the key registration. Check the log for details.
abort.wrong_powerwall: The gateway at that address is a different Powerwall from the one chosen on the Tesla account.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: The gateway at that address is a different Powerwall.

dispatch_battery_power.name: Dispatch battery power
dispatch_battery_power.description: Run the battery at a fixed power for a set time over the signed local connection. Positive watts discharge, negative watts charge, 0 holds the battery idle. Overrides the backup reserve and export setting. The integration renews the command every minute in short steps, so the Powerwall returns to normal within 5 minutes if Home Assistant stops. A new call replaces a running dispatch.

config_entry_id.description: Only needed when more than one Powerwall is set up.

power_watts.name: Power
power_watts.description: Battery power in watts: positive discharges, negative charges (up to 10,000).

duration_seconds.name: Duration
duration_seconds.description: How long to hold this power, in seconds (up to 24 hours).

min_soc.name: Stop discharging at
min_soc.description: End a discharge when the battery level (Tesla app scale) falls to this percentage.

max_soc.name: Stop charging at
max_soc.description: End a charge when the battery level (Tesla app scale) reaches this percentage.

resume_battery_operation.name: Resume battery operation
resume_battery_operation.description: End a dispatch now and hand the battery back to the Powerwall's normal mode.

powerwall_alert.title: Powerwall alert: {description}
powerwall_alert.description:
The Powerwall has reported **{alert}** ({description}) since {since} UTC.

Short alerts like this are normal while the Powerwall restarts or after its On/Off switch is used; this one has lasted more than 10 minutes. Check the Tesla app. If it does not clear, contact your installer or Tesla. This notice disappears when the alert clears.
